primary_source.title: A Blind Spot in Alignment: Quantifying Biosecurity Risks in Large Language Models
primary_source.source_scope: Appendix O OOD Prompt Robustness Analysis, Tables 26-27 and small-sample uncertainty discussion.

verified_claims.claim: On the same 50-prompt stress set, GPT-5 FHR is 2.0% on original prompts and 50.0/52.0/40.0/44.0% under persona, synonym substitution, intent concealment, and keyword removal.
GPT-5-Mini FHR is 0.0% on originals and 40.0/46.0/24.0/58.0% under the same four transformations.
Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Claude-Opus-4.6 are reported at FHR 0.0% across all four strategies.

ShieldGemma-9B detection falls from 50.9% on originals to 0.0% under all four paraphrase strategies; Qwen3Guard-8B is 52.0% original and 2.0/4.0/0.0/2.0%; Llama-Guard-3-8B is 84.5% original and 12.0/52.0/0.0/8.0%.
BioSafe-Guard is 98.9% original detection and 96.0/96.0/92.0/80.0% under persona, synonym substitution, intent concealment, and keyword removal.

reported_uncertainty_examples: GPT-5 synonym-substitution FHR 52.0% with Wilson 95% CI [38.5%, 65.2%]
GPT-5-Mini keyword-removal FHR 58.0% with Wilson 95% CI [44.2%, 70.6%]
additional_primary_source_context.metric_definition_scope: FHR is the paper's Functional Harmfulness Rate from the SPIKE funnel, not generic harmfulness or generic jailbreak ASR.

scope_corrections: The result is a specialized biosecurity/protein-design evaluation. It does not establish that the same paraphrase sensitivities hold in unrelated safety domains.
Each OOD cell has only 50 prompts. The paper reports Wilson intervals and the qualitative gaps are large, but individual percentages should not be treated as high-precision population constants.

The positive-control contrast matters: paraphrase brittleness is not universal across all tested models, and the specialized BioSafe-Guard remains substantially more robust than the three general-purpose guardrails in this stress test.
FHR and input-guard detection are different axes and should not be conflated: the model table measures downstream functional harmfulness, while Table 27 measures guard detection.

assessment.failure_mode: canonical-surface safety can be a support artifact; semantically related prompt transformations can expose materially different functional-risk or detection outcomes
assessment.recommended_downstream_wording: In SPIKE-Bench's 50-prompt paraphrase stress test, some high-refusal models and general-purpose input guardrails degrade sharply under meaning-preserving surface changes, while tested Claude models and BioSafe-Guard provide positive controls showing that the brittleness is not universal. Preserve FHR's biosecurity-specific meaning and the n=50-per-condition scope.
